statement: Which of the following is equivalent to $(2x - 3)(x + 4)$?

choices.misconception: I multiplied only the first terms and the last terms, $2x \cdot x$ and $-3 \cdot 4$, and skipped the two middle products.
I found the middle products $8x$ and $-3x$ but added $8x + 3x$, losing the negative sign on the $3x$.
I mixed up which middle product was negative and combined them as $3x - 8x = -5x$.

hints: Multiply each term in the first binomial by each term in the second.
There are four products: $2x \cdot x$, $2x \cdot 4$, $-3 \cdot x$ and $-3 \cdot 4$. Then combine like terms.
The products are $2x^2$, $8x$, $-3x$ and $-12$. Combine $8x$ and $-3x$.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
